title: Prototype query-global evidence selection and local capability verification
description: Follow-up to TASK-260. Keep the frozen FTS5/RRF retriever and TASK-260 truth/results unchanged and use them only as labeled development data. Build a separate query-global evidence selector that allocates up to three sources across the candidate task set using clause coverage, proof-role demand, non-redundancy, task linkage, path health, and temporal quality. Compare it with the fixed two-per-task selector. Separately test a bounded visible local/Pi helper as a capability verifier on one existing compact packet at a time, measuring positive task decisions, no-match false positives, context, latency, and scope. Do not download models, modify Pi authority, add embeddings, or integrate into startup, routing, UI, canonical authority, or external services.
acceptance_criteria: TASK-259 retriever and TASK-260 truth/results remain byte-for-byte unchanged; the new selector is a separate disposable layer and TASK-260 is labeled development data rather than fresh evidence.

A deterministic query-global selector allocates at most three resolved sources across selected candidate tasks and scores clause coverage, requested proof roles, non-redundancy, task linkage, and temporal attribution without forcing different roles.

Focused tests cover three-role single-task questions, compound cross-task allocation, complementary same-role evidence, unresolved/shared-source penalties, deterministic ordering, and the fixed-selector comparison.

A visible bounded local/Pi verifier receives one frozen TASK-260 packet at a time without repository search or writes; the report records task/no-match decisions, false positives, context, latency, scope, and whether local verification is viable.

The report compares exact-source visibility against TASK-260 15/20, documents abstention/verifier tradeoffs and limitations, freezes a candidate for a later fresh holdout, and makes no integration or embedding claim.
